title: File Locksmith: Handle enumeration can freeze the system and crash with heap corruption
author: jiripolasek

status.label: Covered by open File Locksmith PR
status.detail: The reporter follow-up already links the active pull request that removes the unsafe watchdog path from File Locksmith handle enumeration.

next_action.label: Post linked-fix response
next_action.reason: Keep follow-up on PR 49966 instead of creating a competing design.

judgment.rationale: The issue already has a concrete upstream implementation attempt: PR 49966 is open, explicitly closes issue 49789, and carries the same detached-thread/TerminateThread root-cause analysis described in the reporter follow-up.
evidence: The issue body reports File Locksmith hangs followed by a crash during handle enumeration.
The only public follow-up independently reproduces the crash and explains why the detached worker/TerminateThread path can corrupt memory instead of recovering.
The live issue cross-references open PR 49966, titled '[File Locksmith] Stop terminating the handle-enumeration worker'.
PR 49966 states that it closes issue 49789 and changes FileLocksmithLibInterop/NtdllExtensions.cpp.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep investigation on PR 49966 and avoid a second parallel fix design from the dashboard.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open PR 49966 is the concrete upstream fix attempt for this crash: it replaces the unsafe watchdog termination path with a safe abandonment strategy in File Locksmith handle enumeration.

issue_context.summary: File Locksmith can hang and crash while enumerating handles; the reporter follow-up already escalated the root cause into an open upstream PR.
known_information: The report targets File Locksmith on PowerToys 0.100.2.
The issue describes a crash during handle enumeration and cites heap-corruption style failures.
The follow-up comment reproduces the crash repeatedly and links a patch that removes the unsafe recovery path.
The live issue links open PR 49966.
inferences: The active implementation is already grounded in the same root-cause theory the dashboard would otherwise propose.
A second dashboard-authored design would duplicate active upstream work instead of reducing uncertainty.
issue_context.analysis: This is no longer an unowned bug. The issue already has concrete code, current review state, and reproductions attached to PR 49966, so the most useful artifact is a maintainer-facing handoff to that PR rather than another design prompt.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body, the single detailed follow-up comment, and the live cross-references.
Read PR 49966's summary, open state, and changed-file list to confirm that it targets the same watchdog path.

actions.label: Post linked File Locksmith PR response

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed reproduction and the follow-up analysis. This issue is already linked to PR #49966, which removes the unsafe thread-termination recovery path in File Locksmith handle enumeration and replaces it with a safe abandonment path. That PR is the concrete fix attempt for this crash, so a separate competing design is not needed here. Please keep further validation on PR #49966.
